approach: Teach the possessive adjectives, the rule that they agree with the thing owned (not the owner), the many meanings of su and how to make it clear, and vuestro for recognition.
coverage: mi, mis (my); tu, tus (your, to a friend); su, sus (his, her, its, your formal, their)
Possessives agree with the thing owned: mis padres, nuestra casa
tu (your) has no accent; tú (you) does
su can mean his, her, your or their; to be clear: la casa de él, de ella, de usted, de ellos
vuestro (your, plural informal) is used in Spain; Latin America uses su

data.caption: Possessive adjectives
data.footnote: Spain also uses vuestro, vuestra (your, to a group of friends). In Latin America it is su.

blocks.purpose: States the agreement rule for possessives.

data.ruleName: Agree with the thing, not the owner
data.anchor: A possessive agrees with the thing that is owned, never with the person who owns it.
prerequisites: mis padres: plural, because padres is plural (even though "I" is one person).
nuestra casa: feminine, because casa is feminine (even if "we" are men).
Only nuestro also changes for gender; mi, tu and su change only for number.

data.title: My, your, our
data.cueNote: Su esposa could be his wife, your wife or their wife: context tells you which.

blocks.purpose: Explains the ambiguity of su and how to clear it up.

data.flagIntro: Su (and sus) can mean his, her, its, your (usted or ustedes) or their.

cautions.title: Make it clear with de
cautions.detail: When context is not enough, use the + noun + de + person.
cautions.rightExample: Es el carro de ella. / Es el carro de usted.

cautions.title: tu or tú
cautions.detail: tu (no accent) is your; tú (accent) is you.

blocks.purpose: Practices agreement with the thing owned.

data.title: Choose the possessive
data.instructions: Choose the form that agrees with the thing owned.

feedback.incorrect: At least one choice is off. Change it and check again.

blocks.purpose: Targets agreeing the possessive with the owner.

data.question: Two brothers talk about the house they share. Which is correct?

trapReasons.1: The owners are men, so a masculine form seems right.
trapReasons.2: There are two owners, so a plural seems right.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: In English "our" never changes, so learners look at who owns the thing.
data.correctReasoning: Nuestro agrees with casa, which is feminine singular: nuestra casa.

blocks.purpose: Closes with the forms and the agreement rule.

data.takeaway: Mi, tu, su add -s for more than one thing; nuestro also agrees in gender; all of them agree with the thing owned: mis padres, nuestra casa.

checks.rationale: Padres is plural, so the possessive is plural too: mis padres.
Hijas is feminine plural, so nuestro becomes nuestras.

checks.prompt: "Es su carro" could mean several things. Rewrite it to say clearly "It is HER car": Es el carro ___ ___.
checks.rationale: To make su clear, use de + the person: el carro de ella.
